glosses: To get free; to free oneself.

examples.text: The prisoners escaped by jumping over a wall.
The factory was evacuated after toxic gases escaped from a pipe.

glosses: To avoid (any unpleasant person or thing); to elude, get away from.

examples.text: The children climbed out of the window to escape the fire.
He only got a fine and so escaped going to jail.
sailors that escaped the wreck

glosses: To avoid capture; to get away with something, avoid punishment.

examples.text: Luckily, I escaped with only a fine.

glosses: To elude the observation or notice of; to not be seen or remembered by.

examples.text: The name of the hotel escapes me at present.
The detective examined the crime scene, but one clue escaped his notice.

glosses: To cause (a single character, or all such characters in a string) to be interpreted literally, instead of with any special meaning it would usually have in the same context, often by prefixing with another character.

examples.text: When using the "bash" shell, you can escape the ampersand character with a backslash.

If the data for a URI component would conflict with the reserved purpose, then the conflicting data must be escaped before forming the URI.
Character Data tags allow you to place complex strings as the text of an element—without the need to manually escape the string.

glosses: To leave without being noticed.

examples.text: I'm going to try to slip away from work early, if I can.

1906, Edith Nesbit, The Railway Children, Chapter 4: The engine-burglar,
But when Bobbie crept down later to bring up her presents--for she felt she really could not be separated from them all night--Mother was not writing, but leaning her head on her arms and her arms on the table. I think it was rather good of Bobbie to slip quietly away, saying over and over, "She doesn't want me to know she's unhappy, and I won't know; I won't know." But it made a sad end to the birthday.

When I'm tired and thinking cold

glosses: To pass quickly, almost unnoticed.

examples.text: The months slipped away and became years.

glosses: To disappear; to elude one; to recede; to dwindle.

glosses: Se sauver des mains de quelqu’un, d’une prison, de quelque péril, etc.

examples.text: La partie basse de New York ne fut bientôt plus qu’une fournaise d’où nul n’avait chance d’échapper.
En pleine mer, des bâtiments sombrèrent, ou, désemparés par la tempête, n’échappèrent au naufrage que par des efforts inouïs.

glosses: Ne pas saisir ; laisser sortir.

examples.text: Votre observation m’avait d’abord échappé.

glosses: Ne pas saisir ; laisser sortir.

examples.text: Il est fuyant, il échappe.

glosses: Cesser, par la force ou par la fuite, par un mouvement violent ou adroit, d’être où l’on était, où l’on était retenu.

examples.text: Échapper des mains des ennemis.

glosses: N’être pas saisi, aperçu, découvert, ou seulement remarqué.
